summary: Mail now goes to the messages shard as a stream item when its recipient's host reads stream mail, and stays a graph message.sent claim otherwise (db break-up step 4c-2b). The recipient's host is the member its seat's declaration places it on. It reads stream mail when it is the sending member or its current start advertises messages_stream_inbox=1 (v0.3.30 and later). Routed: an agent's or the daemon's plain message (POST /v1/messages without in_reply_to; fault, missing-product, session-start, idle-nudge, run-report and subscription-batch messages; the account-limits notice and a watch's final wake, through the outbox). Unchanged: replies, work wakes, a person's or an assistant's message, messages with attachments, a delivery probe's mail, alerts and clears (proven by their graph claims), and senders whose message cites other claims. A seat's own poll of its mail, the reconciler and the replication dialers now see routed mail as promptly as graph mail.

replay.detail: No claim is admitted or projected differently. A routed message is a stream item, admitted and replicated as the messages shard already admits a peer's, and every member since v0.3.30 lists, counts and dedupes it.

schema.detail: No table, index, trigger or user_version change.

rules.detail: Where a message.sent is written now depends on its recipient: a stream item when the recipient's declared host is this member or advertises messages_stream_inbox, a graph claim when the member has no shard or is leaving its fleet (a send while leaving is a claim its leave does not fence), the message is a person's or an assistant's, has attachments or is tagged as a delivery probe's (delivery-probe*), the recipient has no host (a person, an undeclared or retired seat), or the host does not advertise the inbox. A stream append that fails for any reason but idempotency-mismatch falls back to the graph append, which checks the stream first, so it never doubles a message. A queued outbox message is routed again when it drains.

compatibility.detail: A member of v0.3.30 lists, counts, delivers and dedupes routed stream mail and routes none of its own sends; upgraded in place it routes. A member of v0.3.29 or earlier never advertises messages_stream_inbox, so no mail routes to its seats, and every member writes graph claims for them. Configured peers count beside fleet members, as for the shard's own peer list.

recovery.detail: Rolling a member back to v0.3.30 is safe: v0.3.30 lists, counts, delivers and dedupes the stream mail routed to its seats, and its new sends are graph claims. Rolling back to v0.3.29 or earlier is NOT safe for a member whose seats were sent routed mail: those releases do not list or count stream mail in their phone lists, unread counts or idle and held indexes, so that mail drops out of them until the member upgrades again. The rollback floor is v0.3.30: to go below it, first roll every member to v0.3.30, so no new mail routes, and let the routed mail be read and closed. A backup carries the messages shard, as since 4c-1, so routed mail is restored with it.
